items.t: Axell hits limit-up on upward earnings revision and dividend hike; Nexon plunges on ex-dividend day in Japan
sum: On September 29, the Tokyo stock market saw buying concentrated in stocks that had announced upward earnings revisions or dividend hikes the previous day, while stocks hit by dividend ex-rights or disappointing clinical trial results were sold off heavily. Axell (6730.T), which makes graphics LSIs for pachinko and pachislot machines, hit limit-up with proportional allocation, while gaming giant Nexon (3659.T) plunged on the ex-rights date for its special dividend.

Axell significantly revised upward its consolidated earnings forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027 the previous day. First-half operating profit was raised from the previous forecast of ¥970 million to ¥1.33 billion (approximately $6.2 million to $8.4 million), and full-year operating profit from ¥1.2 billion to ¥2.29 billion (approximately $7.6 million to $14.5 million). The revision reflects stronger-than-planned sales prospects for graphics LSIs and memory modules for pachinko and pachislot machines. Although the first quarter posted a profit decline, the company expects to benefit from sales price adjustments amid a global surge in memory prices driven by expanding generative AI demand.

Along with the earnings upside, the annual dividend was also significantly raised from the previous plan of ¥41 to ¥79 per share. The stock hit limit-up with proportional allocation at ¥1,526, up ¥300 from the previous day, a gain of 24.5%.

Nexon plunged ¥442.5 to ¥2,625.5. The day marked the ex-rights date for the September-end dividend. The company has a December fiscal year-end but planned a special dividend of ¥415 per share to reduce excess capital, which represented a dividend yield of 15.5% based on the previous day's closing price. This surplus dividend is viewed as a one-time measure, and selling pressure related to the ex-rights adjustment dominated trading.
The ex-rights impact also spread to September fiscal year-end stocks. Noevir Holdings (4928.T), Yokorei (2874.T), and FPG (7148.T) were among the notable decliners.
Biopharmaceutical developer MediciNova (4875.T) hit limit-down with proportional allocation at ¥292, down ¥80 from the previous day.

Roche drops muscle-sparing obesity antibody after flunked interim analysis
sum: Roche has slammed the brakes on an obesity antibody after the candidate showed little hope of hitting its endpoints in a phase 2 study. The Swiss pharma has handed emugrobart back to its Japanese subsidiary Chugai, which will resume development of the molecule for a rare genetic disease while also seeking potential partners.

Emugrobart is meant to block the activity of myostatin, a protein that acts as a check on muscle growth. By inhibiting myostatin and pairing with a GLP-1 like Lilly’s tirzepatide, emugrobart was designed to help patients retain muscle while losing weight.
However, an interim analysis of the phase 2 Gyminda trial of this idea concluded that success was unlikely, Chugai announced today, prompting Roche to give up on the candidate for good.

Trouble first started brewing for emugrobart back in March when the antibody failed to boost muscle growth in trials for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) and facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD). Roche’s Genentech announced the decision to stop development in these diseases in separate letters to the patient communities, after finding that “emugrobart did not consistently deliver the hoped-for improvements in muscle growth and function.”

Muscle loss is a major side effect of weight loss drugs like tirzepatide and Novo’s semaglutide, and multiple biotechs are competing to develop next-gen drugs that help shed pounds without sacrificing muscle in the process. Aside from Roche, AstraZeneca, Biohaven and Wave Life Sciences are also active in the space.
With emugrobart back with Chugai, the biotech plans to take another look at the antibody’s potential in SMA, according to the release.

“Chugai has identified an opportunity to support a phase III study in SMA,” the company said, based on emugrobart’s safety profile, dosing and efficacy data so far. “Chugai has therefore initiated preparations to resume development, while also exploring potential out-licensing opportunities with third parties.”

How an Original Idea Took Shape: The Journey of the Bispecific Antibody Research That Led to the Lasker Award
sum: Hemophilia is a condition in which the blood does not clot easily, so that once bleeding starts — after an injury or a bruise, for example — it is difficult to stop. Hemophilia A in particular is caused by a deficiency of Factor VIII, a protein required for blood to coagulate. More than 20 years ago, researchers at Chugai took on a different challenge: “Rather than replacing the deficient factor itself, could its function be substituted with an antibody?” That idea was the starting point of research into a bispecific antibody for hemophilia A. This research has now been recognized with the Lasker Award (the Lasker-DeBakey Clinical Medical Research Award), one of the world’s most prestigious honors in medicine. What kind of research was it? And why was it recognized by a world-renowned medical award? Tracing the story behind its development, we explore its scientific significance together with the words of the three Chugai researchers who received the award: Kunihiro Hattori (former Senior Fellow of Chugai), Takehisa Kitazawa (Deputy Head of Research Division, Chugai) and Tomoyuki Igawa (Head of Research Division, Chugai).

This article is intended to introduce the research recognized by a medical research award and the scientific significance of that research. The content explains the historical and academic background of the research and development, and is not intended to recommend, evaluate or provide information about any specific pharmaceutical product or treatment. For decisions regarding treatment, please always consult a healthcare professional.

People with hemophilia A are born with a deficiency of Factor VIII, the protein needed for blood to clot, and so their blood does not coagulate easily. In our bodies, platelets first gather to stop bleeding, which is known as primary hemostasis, and several blood coagulation factors then work together to form a firm clot, which is known as secondary hemostasis. In hemophilia A, Factor VIII, which is required for this secondary hemostasis, is deficient. As a result, when bleeding occurs after an injury or a bruise, it can take time for the bleeding to stop, and bleeding may recur even once it has stopped.

items.t: Sep 07,2026 | Sponsoring the
sum: Chugai Pharmaceutical sponsors the “Chugai Pharmaceutical 2026 Family Chair Ski Program,” an initiative for children with disabilities and their families. Organized by the Japan Chair Ski Association, the program was held for the 11th consecutive year in 2026. This year, sessions took place at five ski resorts across Japan: Miyagi Zao Eboshi Ski Resort (Miyagi Prefecture), Hunter Mountain Shiobara (Tochigi Prefecture), Maiko Snow Resort (Niigata Prefecture), Yuzawa Nakazato Snow Resort (Niigata Prefecture), and Kiroro Resort (Hokkaido), with a total of 122 families participating.

During the program, participants set goals aligned with their individual abilities and challenged themselves to achieve them. The experience provided opportunities for children to build confidence through taking on new challenges, while families and peers offered support and encouragement. Through these shared experiences, participants fostered greater independence, resilience, and stronger connections with those around them.

By supporting this initiative, Chugai contributes to creating inclusive opportunities for people of all abilities to enjoy sports in the same environment. The program helps foster self-esteem and a willingness to take on new challenges while promoting social inclusion through sport.

Chugai Pharmaceutical remains committed to supporting adaptive sports initiatives that enable children with disabilities to expand their horizons, realize their potential, and participate more fully in society.

sum: TOKYO, August 3, 2026 -- Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (TOKYO: 4519) announced today that it will become a “Healthcare Innovation Partner” of the Japan Basketball Association (JBA; Bunkyo-ku, Tokyo; President: Shinji Shimada).

JBA is guided by its vision, “Energizing Japan Through Basketball!”, and strives to create vitality across Japan through the growth and challenges of everyone involved in the sport. Chugai's mission is to create new value through the provision of innovative medicines and services, thereby contributing to healthcare and the health of people around the world, with the ultimate goal of helping people lead healthier and more fulfilling lives.

There is a shared spirit of challenge between the Japan national basketball team, AKATSUKI JAPAN, competing on the global stage, and Chugai's commitment to continually pursuing new challenges in creating innovative medicines. Inspired by the belief that such challenges can bring energy and hope to society, Chugai and JBA have agreed to embark on this partnership.
Through this partnership, Chugai will contribute to the promotion and development of basketball in Japan while working together with JBA to create new value at the intersection of sports and health.
Comment from Osamu Okuda, President and CEO, Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd.

We are honored to support AKATSUKI JAPAN as a partner of the Japan Basketball Association. We deeply resonate with JBA's efforts to promote the healthy physical and mental development of people and to help build a prosperous society through basketball.

Athletes competing on the global stage often face formidable obstacles. Yet, while keeping their eyes on the goals beyond those challenges, they continue striving forward. Their dedication not only brings courage and inspiration to people, but also helps foster bonds among teammates and encourages others to take the first step toward new challenges.

items.t: Shin-Etsu Chemical Plunges as Full-Year Outlook Misses ¥760 Billion Market Forecast; Chugai Pharmaceutical Also Disappoints
sum: On Monday the 27th, the Tokyo stock market saw a stark divergence in the performance of major companies that reported quarterly earnings the previous weekend. Shin-Etsu Chemical (4063.T) and Chugai Pharmaceutical (4519.T) both fell sharply, while select information services and airline sector stocks attracted buying interest.

Shin-Etsu Chemical shares extended their decline sharply, falling ¥556 from the previous weekend's close to ¥6,146. The company's first-quarter (April-June) results for the fiscal year ending March 2027 showed operating profit rose 4.2% year-on-year to ¥173.8 billion (approximately $1.1 billion), roughly in line with market expectations. However, the company maintained its full-year operating profit forecast at ¥700 billion (approximately $4.3 billion), up 10.2% from the previous fiscal year, which disappointed investors. The figure significantly undershoots the market consensus of around ¥760 billion (approximately $4.6 billion), triggering selling driven by disappointment.

While supply and demand for semiconductor silicon wafers remain tight, the outlook for the living environment and infrastructure materials segment—including subsidiary Shin-Etsu Polymer, which handles polyvinyl chloride resin—is seen as more cautious than the market had anticipated, contributing to the earnings forecast falling short of expectations.

Chugai Pharmaceutical also fell sharply in a significant pullback, ending the session at ¥6,848, down ¥568 from the previous weekend. The company's core operating profit for the second quarter (April-June) of the fiscal year ending December 2026 was ¥165.9 billion (approximately $1.0 billion), up 25.2% year-on-year, but appeared to miss market estimates by about 5%. Cumulative first-half (January-June) results totaled ¥329.1 billion (approximately $2.0 billion), putting the run rate slightly below 50% of the full-year forecast of ¥670 billion (approximately $4.1 billion).

Market observers attributed Chugai Pharmaceutical's earnings shortfall to lower-than-expected sales of the hemophilia treatment Hemlibra to Swiss pharmaceutical giant Roche, as well as royalty income from the oral obesity treatment Foundayo remaining at low levels.
